title: X-ray Spectral Softening in AO 0235+164: Swift-XRT Analysis and Class-S Classification (C3 Complete Sample Final)
abstract: Systematic Swift-XRT hardness ratio analysis of AO 0235+164 (ISP BL Lac, z=0.94) using 180 observations (63,028 photons) spanning 2007–2024. Result: β=−0.682, r=−0.434, p=1.14×10⁻⁹ → Class-S (spectral softening). This completes the C3 Complete Sample Classification: 11 ISP BL Lac objects from 4LAC-DR3 high, H:1 (TXS 0506+056, neutrino-confirmed) / S:10, total 277,743 photons. Probability by chance ≈0.6%. Predicts future neutrino-emitting blazars will exhibit Class-H (spectral hardening) behavior
keywords: blazar, ISP BL Lac, Swift-XRT, AO 0235+164, neutrino, IceCube, spectral variability, Class-S, 4LAC, X-ray spectroscopy

title: Complete X-Ray Spectral Classification of ISP Blazars in the 4LAC-DR3 High-Variability Sample: A Ten-Source Swift-XRT Hardness Ratio Study and the Class-S/H Neutrino Prediction Framework
abstract: We present the complete X-ray spectral classification of all 10 ISP BL Lac objects in the 4LAC-DR3 high-variability blazar sample using Swift-XRT hardness ratio analysis. Total: 214,715 photons across ~191 observations (2005–2023). Result: 9/10 sources are Class-S (spectral softening, leptonic), 1/10 (TXS 0506+056) is Class-H (spectral hardening, hadronic) — the only confirmed astrophysical neutrino blazar. title: Complete Class-S/H Classification of the C3 ISP Blazar Sample: All 10 Sources via Swift-XRT Hardness Ratio Analysis
abstract: We present the complete X-ray spectral classification of all 10 ISP BL Lac objects in the 4LAC-DR3 high-variability sample using Swift-XRT hardness ratio (HR) analysis. The C3 (Complete Classification of C3) sample comprises: TXS 0506+056 (Class-H, confirmed neutrino source), and 9 Class-S sources (W Comae, S5 0716+714, 3C 66A, ON 246, PKS 0735+178, PKS B1424-418, MG1 J021114+1051, PMN J0531-4827, TXS 1055+567). title: X-Ray Spectral Softening in the IceCube HESE-35 Candidate Blazar PKS B1424-418: A Class-S Classification via Swift-XRT Hardness Ratio Analysis
abstract: We present a systematic Swift-XRT hardness ratio (HR) analysis of PKS B1424-418 (z=0.452), proposed as a counterpart to IceCube HESE-35 ('Big Bird', ~2013 April, PeV-scale neutrino). Using 73 archival PC-mode observations spanning 2005–2023 (total N=95,313 photons), we find β=−0.696 (r=−0.762, p=4.87×10⁻¹⁵) in HR vs. count rate — firmly Class-S (spectral softening). keywords: blazar, PKS B1424-418, IceCube HESE-35, Big Bird, Swift-XRT, hardness ratio, neutrino, multimessenger astronomy, Class-S, spectral classification, X-ray astronomy

title: X-Ray Spectral Softening in the IceCube-211208A Candidate Blazar PKS 0735+178: A Class-S Classification via Swift-XRT Hardness Ratio Analysis
abstract: Systematic Swift-XRT hardness ratio analysis of PKS 0735+178 (z=0.424), a proposed counterpart to IceCube-211208A (separation 2.2°). Using 24 archival PC-mode observations spanning 2009–2022 (N=14,917 photons), we find β=−0.706 (r=−0.579, p=3.0×10⁻³) in HR vs. count rate, classifying PKS 0735+178 as Class-S (spectral softening at high flux). title: Quasi-Periodic Oscillations in C3 ISP Blazars: Evidence from Fermi-LAT FAVA 17-Year Light Curves
abstract: We present a Lomb-Scargle periodicity analysis of five Intermediate-frequency Peaked BL Lac objects (ISP blazars) belonging to the C3 clustering group, using 17 years (2008–2025) of weekly Fermi-LAT FAVA σ-excess light curves. All five sources exhibit statistically significant quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) with false alarm probabilities ranging from 5.8×10⁻⁴ to 1.3×10⁻²⁶. title: Detection-Limit Hypothesis: N_min ∝ Fvar² — Empirical Verification Across Five C3 ISP Blazars
abstract: We present empirical verification of the Detection-Limit Hypothesis using Swift XRT archival data from five C3 ISP blazars (ON 246, 3C 66A, TXS 0506+056, W Comae, S5 0716+714). The hypothesis states that the minimum photon count N_min required to statistically detect a given spectral change |ΔHR| scales as N_min ∝ Fvar², where Fvar is the fractional variability amplitude. title: Statistical Substructure of ISP Blazar Variability: Five-Source Analysis and Class-S/Class-H Spectral Bifurcation
abstract: Five-source Swift XRT analysis of C3 ISP blazars. TXS 0506+056 (15,690 photons) and S5 0716+714 (33,064 photons) added to the three-source v6 sample. Reveals spectral bifurcation: Class-S (softening, 4/5 sources, leptonic) vs Class-H (hardening, TXS 0506+056, hadronic candidate). TXS 0506+056 shows ΔHR = +0.199, p = 0.0029, KS p = 0.0015. Detection-Limit Hypothesis quantified as N_min ∝ Fvar². Predicts neutrino-emitting blazars preferentially exhibit Class-H X-ray spectral behavior.
keywords: blazars, ISP, Swift XRT, TXS 0506+056, S5 0716+714, IceCube, neutrino, Class-H, hadronic, 4LAC-DR3
